subject.title: Feature: config-level default task notify policy

question: Should OpenClaw add a public config-level default task notify policy, and should that policy be global or per runtime type?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but this adds a user-visible config/default contract that can change channel message volume and overlaps narrower visibility/spam reports.

options.title: Approve Per-Runtime Defaults
options.body: Add an unset-by-default `agents.defaults.tasks.notifyPolicy` map for ACP, subagent, cron, and CLI so current behavior remains the default while operators can silence or expand specific runtimes.

options.title: Approve One Global Default
options.body: Add one simpler default policy for task records while documenting that explicit task, cron, CLI, and media policies still override it.

options.title: Defer Config Surface
options.body: Leave this open and address only narrower channel/runtime issues until maintainers choose a broader task-notification policy.

recommendation.title: Approve Per-Runtime Defaults
recommendation.body: Add an unset-by-default `agents.defaults.tasks.notifyPolicy` map for ACP, subagent, cron, and CLI so current behavior remains the default while operators can silence or expand specific runtimes.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and related subagent/config policy history make steipete the strongest routing candidate for the public config/default decision.
